phase2.alfred_records_not_agency_first_release: Real-time values come from ALFRED's records, which may differ from the producing agency's own first release.
phase2.alternative_classification_concordance_r: The alternative productive-sector classification is mapped to WIOD industries by a reviewed transcription, not by the authors.
phase2.announcement_dates_not_published_before_: NBER publishes committee announcement dates only from 1979; earlier turning points have no public announcement date, so they cannot be dated to when they were known.
phase2.archived_factsheet_months_missing: Only months whose MSCI factsheet the Internet Archive captured are observed; the other months are absent, not filled.
phase2.capture_time_bounds_dissemination: Each value is dated by the document's own as-of month; when MSCI actually published it is known only up to the archive capture time.
phase2.country_weights_top_n_only: MSCI factsheets print only the largest countries plus 'Other'; full country weights are not freely published.
phase2.deferred_research_extension: This analysis is a deferred research extension outside Phase 2 completion; the reason is given with it.
phase2.dimensions_as_declared_in_catalogue: Population, currency and price basis are as declared in the series catalogue, without a separate cited review.
phase2.exact_original_inputs_missing_or_partial: Some required original inputs are missing or only partly available, so the analysis cannot be computed in full.
phase2.exact_source_unavailable_fallback_used: The preferred source is unavailable, so a cited fallback source is used in its place.
phase2.history_starts_with_archive_captures: History begins only where archived captures begin, so early months are missing; the coverage is given with it.
phase2.holdings_field_not_reported_by_publisher: Some holdings fields (for example sector or identifiers) are not reported by the fund's publisher, so those breakdowns are incomplete.
phase2.holdings_weights_only_accounting_control: Holdings are reconciled only through their portfolio weights, not through reported market values.
phase2.io_input_origin_share_author_published: The input-origin ratio is the authors' published value, not yet recomputed from the WIOD input-output tables.
phase2.latest_revised_values_not_real_time: Values are the publisher's latest revised figures, not what was known at the time.
phase2.market_observation_assumed_unrevised: Market observations are treated as unrevised once published; no vintage history exists to confirm it.
phase2.no_approved_analysis_window_common_nativ: No specific time window is set for this comparison; its inputs are matched over the full period they all cover.
phase2.original_comparison_open: Not every role is covered by a verified original comparison yet.
phase2.original_scientific_failure: At least one input failed a scientific check against its original source.
phase2.printed_value_conflicts_blocked: Where two documents print different values for the same index and month, that month is left out; neither value is used.
phase2.publisher_absent_periods_excluded_from_j: Periods the publisher does not report (or that only some inputs report) are left out of the matched comparison; nothing is filled.
phase2.publisher_matrix_residuals_within_materi: The publisher's input-output tables do not balance exactly; residuals within the materiality bound are kept, not rebalanced.
phase2.publisher_page_header_date_typo: A publisher page header shows a wrong date; the announcement's own dateline is used instead.
phase2.release_dates_not_published_by_publisher: The publisher keeps no release vintages, so values cannot be dated to when they were first known.
phase2.role_descoped_by_phase1_revision: One input of the original design was removed or replaced by the 2026-11-06 Phase 1 revision; the reason is given with it.
phase2.self_employed_labour_income_imputed_by_p: Self-employed labour income is imputed by WIOD; mixed income is not published separately by industry.
phase2.supervisory_labour_not_separated: Supervisory labour cannot be separated from other labour outside the United States.
phase2.surplus_includes_depreciation: Surplus is gross of depreciation, because the WIOD Socio-Economic Accounts publish no consumption of fixed capital by industry.
phase2.turnover_and_circulating_capital_not_pub: Capital turnover and circulating capital are not published, so profit rates use fixed capital only.
phase2.io_total_value_adds_product_taxes: The input-origin ratio is recomputed from the WIOD input-output tables and matches the authors; their total value counts product taxes twice, as published.
phase2.owner_supplied_values_not_verified: Supplied by your saved portfolio inputs; validated for range and consistency, not checked against any account or publisher.
phase2.curated_shock_register: Shock events come from a curated register, each dated by the official source it cites; not a complete census of shocks.

P06.planning_ranges_not_forecasts: Expected-return estimates are model-based planning ranges, not forecasts or timing signals.
P06.revised_shiller_overlapping_windows: The equity range uses latest revised Shiller data and overlapping windows; V05 evaluates the relationship on real-time data.
P06.yields_approximate_hold_to_maturity: Bond yields approximate nominal returns only when held to maturity; euro AAA curve is model-fitted, not a traded bond.

P07.hedge_cost_cip_approximation: Hedged returns approximate forward points by the ECB deposit-facility minus effective federal funds rate; actual hedge costs, basis and fund fees are not included.
P07.month_end_reference_rates: Month-end values are the last published observation in each month; ECB reference rates are not transaction rates.
P07.index_not_investable_fund: MSCI ACWI net total return in USD is an index, not an investable fund; ETF fees and tracking differences are excluded.

F03.credit_gap_early_warning_only: The credit gap uses BIS's one-sided HP trend; it is an early-warning indicator with false positives, not a crisis forecast.
F03.dsr_own_history_only: Debt-service ratios are compared with each economy's own history; raw levels are not comparable across countries.
F03.no_world_credit_gap: A weighted average of national gaps is not a world credit gap; no aggregate is shown.

C01.cli_direction_not_probability: Leading indicators show the direction of the growth cycle against trend; they are not a recession probability or a timing signal.
C01.clock_month_to_month: The clock uses one-month direction, which can reverse from month to month; the trail shows how settled a move is.
C01.us_only_activity: The activity panels and the grey recession bands are US-only.

C03.different_sources_per_view: Annual growth comes from the World Bank; the world aggregate is the publisher's own, not an average of the regions shown.
C03.dispersion_fixed_cohort: Dispersion is the unweighted spread across the United States, European Union, China, India and Japan, only in years where all five are reported.
C03.growth_not_returns: Faster economic growth has not reliably meant higher equity returns; this is context for regional weights, not a signal to tilt.

C06.weo_history_only: IMF inflation and growth are historical estimates; current-year and forecast years are excluded, and past years may have been revised.
C06.commodity_usd_quotes: Commodity prices are World Bank monthly USD quotes (Brent, US natural gas, maize), not euro prices paid by consumers.
C06.map_is_annual: The stagflation map pairs growth and inflation only in years both are reported; it shows co-movement, not cause.

M01.different_instruments: The Fed line is the effective overnight rate, the ECB line its deposit facility rate and the BoJ line the uncollateralised overnight call rate: comparable short rates, not identical instruments.
M01.monthly_history: History shows the last observation in each month; the ladder uses the latest daily value.
M01.gap_not_hedge_cost: The euro's rate gap approximates the carry of a currency hedge; actual forward points, basis and fees differ.

M02.identity_by_construction: Breakeven here is the nominal minus the real 10-year yield on the same market date, so the split adds up by construction; the published breakeven is shown for comparison.
M02.breakeven_not_forecast: Breakeven inflation includes risk and liquidity premiums; it is not a pure inflation forecast.
M02.us_only: These are US Treasury yields; euro-area inflation-linked yields are not in the free corpus.

M04.coincidence_not_cause: Currency moves and rate gaps are shown side by side; their co-movement is not a causal estimate or a forecast.
M04.ecb_reference_rates: Exchange rates are ECB daily reference rates (last of each month), not transaction rates.
M04.log_change: The euro's move is the 12-month change in the log of the exchange rate, in percent; positive means the euro strengthened.

F01.one_sided_trend: The trend is BIS's one-sided HP filter; it adapts slowly, so long credit booms can pull the trend up behind them.
F01.credit_to_gdp_not_quality: Credit-to-GDP measures quantity, not the quality of lending or who holds the risk.
F01.no_world_aggregate: Economies are compared side by side; no world credit gap is formed.

F02.own_history_only: Debt-service ratios are compared with each economy's own history; levels are not comparable across countries.
F02.bis_estimates: BIS debt-service ratios are model estimates from credit, rates and maturities, not survey measures.
F02.five_year_window: The change compares the latest quarter with the same quarter five years earlier.

F04.stress_now_not_forecast: Stress indexes describe conditions now; they are not forecasts of crashes and not exit signals.
F04.index_zero_average: The NFCI and OFR index are centred on their long-run averages: above zero is tighter or more stressed than usual.
F04.high_yield_archive_join: The high-yield spread joins FRED's own full download archived by the Internet Archive (1996 to November 2025) with FRED's current three years; every shared day agrees exactly, and any disagreement would withhold the join.

F05.different_dates: Household and corporate debt are quarterly BIS figures; government debt is the IMF's annual figure, so its year can lag.
F05.gross_debt: All three are gross debt relative to GDP; assets held against the debt are not netted.
F05.us_banks_only: Bank equity to assets covers US FDIC-insured institutions only.

F06.real_index_levels: Real house prices are BIS indexes deflated by consumer prices; levels are compared with each market's own history, not across countries.
F06.no_valuation_model: Prices against their own history are not a valuation model (rents, incomes and rates are not used here).
F06.portugal_commercial_annual: Portuguese commercial property is annual and starts in 2009.

F07.us_sector_aggregates: These are US Financial Accounts sector totals, not individual firms or funds.
F07.leverage_book_values: Leverage is total assets over equity capital at book values.
F07.context_not_signal: High leverage and repo dependence describe fragility, not timing.

V01.valuation_not_timing: High valuations have meant lower long-run returns on average, but they say little about the next year.
V01.us_only_long_history: The long history is US (Shiller, S&P Composite); world valuation history is short.
V01.excess_yield_definition: Excess CAPE yield = 1/CAPE minus the 10-year TIPS real yield, from 2003 when TIPS data start.

V02.annual_bea_measures: BEA Q ratios are annual and end with the latest published year, later than CAPE.
V02.different_denominators: The three Q measures use different denominators (produced assets, adding bonds, net liquid assets); none is identical to another valuation ratio.
V02.agreement_not_proof: Measures agreeing does not prove mispricing; they share the same market prices.

V03.msci_factsheet_months: Regional P/E comes from archived MSCI factsheets; only captured months exist, so lines are dots, not continuous series.
V03.regions_differ_in_sectors: Regional P/E differences partly reflect different sector mixes, not only cheapness.
V03.forward_is_consensus: Forward P/E uses analysts' consensus earnings for the next 12 months, which tend to be optimistic.

V05.overlapping_windows: Windows overlap heavily; the effective number of independent observations is about windows divided by 12 times the horizon.
V05.revised_data: Shiller data are latest revised values; earnings revisions mean this is not a real-time test.
V05.rank_correlation_only: A rank correlation shows whether cheaper starts ranked better outcomes, not the size of the effect or a forecast.

G05.annual_imf: Current accounts and investment positions are annual IMF figures; the latest year can lag.
G05.position_over_gdp: The net investment position is divided by nominal GDP in US dollars for the same year; currency swings move both.
G05.context_for_currency: Large external deficits or debtor positions are context for currency risk, not a forecast of a currency's direction.

G06.tiva_ends_2022: OECD TiVA shares are annual and currently end in 2022.
G06.share_of_value_added: The share is the part of a country's own value added that ends up in foreign final demand, not its export-to-GDP ratio.
G06.exposure_not_risk: Higher dependence on foreign demand means more exposure to foreign cycles and trade shocks, not necessarily more risk to investors.

L01.same_deflator: Pay and productivity are both deflated by the value-added price index of the same economy, so the gap reflects the labour share, not consumer prices.
L01.average_not_median: Compensation per hour is an average including high earners; median pay grows more slowly where inequality rises.
L01.euklems_scope: EU KLEMS covers the total economy including the self-employed (imputed); BLS covers the US nonfarm business sector.

L02.nonfinancial_corporations: Shares refer to non-financial corporations' gross value added, not the whole economy.
L02.net_surplus_after_depreciation: Net operating surplus is gross surplus minus consumption of fixed capital.
L02.remainder_shown: Where published parts do not add up to value added, the difference is shown as a remainder rather than hidden.

L03.book_capital: The profit rate divides net operating surplus by the net stock of fixed assets at current replacement cost; it is not a return on equity.
L03.different_coverage: Capital stock series start later for some economies, so first years differ.
L03.not_marxian_rate: This is a national-accounts profit rate; Marxian rates (L04) use different labour and capital definitions.

L05.us_only: Wealth distribution is the Federal Reserve's US Distributional Financial Accounts; no comparable free series exists for the euro area.
L05.household_net_worth: Shares are of household net worth, including housing and pensions, not of financial assets only.
L05.quarterly_estimates: Quarterly DFA estimates are revised as source surveys update.

L07.pretax_national_income: Shares are of pre-tax national income (World Inequality Database), before taxes and transfers.
L07.harmonised_estimates: WID series combine tax data, surveys and national accounts; earlier years carry more uncertainty.
L07.world_is_global_distribution: The world row is the global distribution across all individuals, not an average of countries.

P02.us_bonds_proxy: Bonds are the US 10-year sovereign total return (Swinkels), ending in 2022; a free world bond index is not available.
P02.gold_monthly_average: Gold uses monthly average prices, which smooth month-to-month moves and can understate correlations.
P02.correlations_change: Correlations shift between regimes; the 2022 inflation shock is a reminder that stocks and bonds can fall together.

P03.index_not_fund: Drawdowns are of the MSCI ACWI net total return index in US dollars, not a fund in euros; fees and currency are excluded.
P03.threshold_choice: Only falls deeper than 15% are listed; smaller corrections are visible in the underwater chart.

G01.etf_holdings_not_index: Concentration is read from the iShares MSCI ACWI ETF's SEC N-PORT filings, which track the index closely but are not MSCI's own constituent file.
G01.issuer_grouping: Issuers are grouped by their exact reported name; share classes are summed, but parent companies are not merged.
G01.quarterly_filings: Filings are quarterly, so concentration between filing dates is not observed.

G02.country_of_issuer: Country weights follow the issuer's reported country, not where companies earn their revenue; many Chinese companies are registered in the Cayman Islands or Hong Kong, so China's index weight here understates Chinese exposure.
G02.gdp_in_dollars: GDP shares use nominal US-dollar GDP from the World Bank, which moves with exchange rates.
G02.weights_not_a_target: Market-cap weights differing from GDP weights is how index investing works; it is context, not a signal to reweight.

L04.theory_laden: Marxian rates depend on which industries count as productive and how labour income is measured; the spread across variants is the point of this view.
L04.wiod_2000_2014: WIOD covers 2000-2014. EU KLEMS 2025 extends both methods to 2021 for the eight non-Chinese countries, the full method with the input-origin ratio recomputed from OECD ICIO 2025 (within about 0.04 of WIOD's ratio over 2000-2014). Over 2000-2014 the extensions differ from WIOD by up to about 0.05 (value added only) and 0.15 (full method) in the rate of surplus value, most for the United States; the page and export give the gaps per country.
L04.two_value_added_methods: The authors' full method corrects productive value added with the WIOD input-output tables; the value-added-only view shows how much that correction matters. Their total value counts product taxes twice, reproduced as published.
L04.merged_industries_as_bounds: EU KLEMS merges some WIOD industries; a merged industry spanning productive and unproductive activities (M, and E under the alternative classification, M-N in Japan) is counted once each way, never split by imputation.

P01.published_holdings_only: Exposures are read from each fund's own published holdings (SEC N-PORT for VT and BND, the iShares file for the UCITS ETF).
P01.issuer_country: Country is the issuer's reported location, not where revenue is earned.
P01.no_portfolio_weights_yet: Each fund is shown on its own; combining them needs your portfolio weights (owner inputs).

P04.first_order: Shocks are first-order estimates: they ignore convexity, correlations between shocks and how prices respond together.
P04.owner_parameters: Weights, duration, hedging and the euro share of equities are your own inputs; until saved, an example portfolio is used.
P04.single_shocks: Each shock is applied alone; real episodes usually combine several.

P05.history_not_forecast: A replay of one historical path; the order of returns (sequence risk) will differ in future.
P05.simplified_tax: Tax is your chosen simplification: a rate on gains realised when selling (no loss offsets or allowances), or a yearly rate on the whole value (no tax-free allowance). It is not tax advice.
P05.bond_leg: Euro or hedged bonds are a hypothetical German 10-year government bond, rebuilt from the Bundesbank month-end par yield with Swinkels' formula (it reproduces his published series exactly) from 1972; unhedged foreign bonds are the US 10-year sovereign in euros (Swinkels), which ends in 2022.
P05.replay_hedging_scope: The equity replay always uses unhedged USD ACWI translated into EUR. Your equity hedge share, euro-area equity share and bond duration affect P04 shocks only. Selecting euro or hedged bonds uses the German par-bond surrogate, not a hedge of the US bond history.
P05.replay_transaction_order: Each replay month applies returns, adds the contribution, takes a withdrawal of one twelfth of the entered annual percentage of current value, charges any tax on value every 12 replay months, then rebalances and deducts trading costs and realised-gain tax. Trading costs apply to one-sided turnover; cash flows are not charged trading costs. Wealth and drawdown include cash flows, so they are not flow-adjusted investment returns.
P05.simplified_tax_funding: Fees and tax are deducted from holdings with simplified cost basis reductions; extra taxable gains from funding those charges are not recursively modelled. The replay omits loss offsets and allowances and is not a statutory tax calculation.

C02.fixed_windows: An inversion counts as a warning if it starts within 24 months before a recession; a Sahm trigger counts from 12 months before to 18 months after the start. Other windows would move some signals between warning and false alarm.
C02.month_end_spread: The daily yield spread is read at each month's last trading day.
C02.few_recessions: Only five US recessions fall inside the yield-spread history since 1982, too few to estimate how reliable either signal is.
C02.revised_sahm: The Sahm series is FRED's real-time series. It is checked against the Sahm rule recomputed from the Philadelphia Fed's unemployment vintages, collected from the original BLS releases, at each quarterly vintage; months that differ are listed.

C05.peak_window: The pre-recession peak is the highest level in the 12 months before the recession starts; a different window can change depth and recovery times.
C05.revised_levels: Levels are today's revised figures, not what was published at the time.
C05.shocks_as_context: Shock events are listed for context when they fall near a recession; they are not used to define recessions.

G03.non_equivalent: The national-accounts alternatives include listed and unlisted companies and measure gross operating surplus, before depreciation. Net operating surplus would still be before property-income flows and corporation tax; neither is consolidated after-tax listed-parent net profit.
G03.regional_coverage: EU27 covers non-financial corporations; the OECD aggregate uses current 38-member eligibility with changing reporting-country/GDP coverage shown separately. Neither covers the worldwide listed-parent universe.
G03.implied_index_earnings_proxy: ACWI factsheet capitalization divided by P/E is an implied index earnings proxy. MSCI normalizes continuing-operations earnings, applies free-float inclusion factors and excludes missing EPS; matching P/E numerator coverage to total capitalization is unverified. It is not reported company net profit. Proxy / world GDP is arithmetic context. Method: https://www.msci.com/indexes/documents/methodology/0_MSCI_Fundamental_Data_Methodology_20240625.pdf (sections 1.2.2 and 3.1).
